quick: Insert saturated wick; instill 5 drops 3-4 times daily
Minimal systemic absorption; use if needed
summary: Acetic acid otic solution (2%) is a topical acidifying anti-infective used to treat superficial infections of the external ear canal (otitis externa) caused by susceptible bacteria and fungi. Treatment usually begins with an acetic-acid-saturated cotton wick kept moist, followed by instilling 5 drops three to four times daily. It is contraindicated when the tympanic membrane is perforated. Systemic absorption is minimal; the main adverse effects are local stinging, burning, or irritation.
indications: Treatment of superficial infections of the external auditory canal caused by organisms susceptible to acetic acid (otitis externa / swimmer's ear)

dosage.d: Insert a cotton wick saturated with solution; keep moist by adding 3-5 drops every 4-6 hours
Instill 5 drops into the affected ear 3 or 4 times daily
dosage.n: Continue as directed until infection resolves

dosage.d: 3-4 drops may be sufficient due to smaller ear canal capacity

admin: For use in the ear only (otic); do not use in the eye
Carefully remove all cerumen and debris first so the solution can contact infected surfaces directly
For severe inflammation, insert a saturated cotton wick and keep it moist with the solution; remove after 24 hours
Warm the bottle in the hand before instilling and have the patient keep the head tilted for several minutes after dosing
Discontinue promptly if sensitization or irritation occurs
moa: Acetic acid lowers the pH of the external ear canal, creating an acidic environment that is unfavorable to bacterial and fungal growth, thereby exerting antibacterial and antifungal effects. In combination products the propylene glycol vehicle is hydrophilic and provides a low surface tension to spread the solution; some formulations contain hydrocortisone for anti-inflammatory effect.

absolute: Perforated tympanic membrane (any medication in the external ear canal is contraindicated)
Known hypersensitivity to acetic acid or formulation components
relative: Recurrent or chronic otitis where middle-ear involvement is suspected
monitor: Integrity of the tympanic membrane before use

preg: Systemic absorption from otic application is minimal, and significant fetal risk is not expected. Use during pregnancy if needed; combination products containing a corticosteroid warrant the usual caution.
lact: Because systemic absorption from otic use is minimal, acetic acid otic solution is not expected to affect the breastfed infant and is considered compatible with breastfeeding.
renal: Not applicable - acetic acid is applied topically in the ear with minimal systemic absorption; no renal dose adjustment is required.
hepatic: Not applicable - acetic acid is applied topically in the ear with minimal systemic absorption; no hepatic dose adjustment is required.

minor: May be inactivated by alkaline ear preparations applied concurrently

common: Transient stinging or burning on instillation
rare: Local irritation or contact dermatitis of the ear canal

monitoring: Resolution of ear canal infection and symptoms
Local irritation, burning, or signs of sensitization
Confirmation that the tympanic membrane is intact before and during use
Need to reassess if no improvement within the expected time
counsel: For use in the ear only; do not put it in the eye
Clean and dry the ear canal before use as directed
Some brief stinging or burning can occur; report persistent irritation, rash, or swelling
Do not use if you have or suspect a hole (perforation) in the eardrum
Keep the head tilted for a few minutes after instilling so the drops stay in the ear
Keep ears dry; complete the full course even if symptoms improve
pk: Local effect over several hours; dose 3-4 times daily
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); keep container tightly closed
pearls: Acidifying the ear canal makes it hostile to bacteria and fungi - useful for swimmer's ear
Contraindicated if the tympanic membrane is perforated
A medicated wick helps deliver solution when the canal is swollen and edematous
Combination products may add hydrocortisone (anti-inflammatory) or antibiotics
Keep ears dry to prevent recurrence of otitis externa
missed: If a dose is missed, instill it as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the usual schedule. Do not use extra drops to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: Overdose is not a clinically meaningful concern with otic use because systemic absorption is minimal. Accidental ingestion of the solution should be managed supportively. Excess drops or irritation should be addressed by discontinuing use.
